title: Gran Hotel Ciudad de México: Spectre Hotel Guide
description: The Gran Hotel Ciudad de México, with its stained-glass ceiling, appears in Spectre and License to Kill. History and booking tips.
h1: Gran Hotel Ciudad de México: the stained-glass hotel from Spectre
intro: Under a Tiffany-style stained-glass ceiling in Mexico City's historic centre, the Gran Hotel is one of the city's most striking interiors. James Bond has been here twice.
filming: The hotel appears in the James Bond films Spectre (2015) and License to Kill (1989). Its cage-style elevators and lobby feature in Spectre's Mexico City sequence, although the street entrance was shot at another building.
facts: The building was inaugurated in 1899 as a department store, in the Art Nouveau style.
It began operating as a hotel in 1968, just before the Mexican Olympics.
Its glass ceiling was reportedly imported from France in 1908.
The lobby has one of the first panoramic elevators installed in Mexico City.
Its building sits among other Art Nouveau landmarks of the Mexican capital, such as the Palacio de Bellas Artes.
visit: The hotel is in the historic centre, a short walk from the Zócalo and the city's major landmarks. The lobby is open to look at, so it is worth a visit even for a quick coffee, and the stained-glass ceiling is best seen from the ground floor.
